summary: Yasuro Abe works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako and Otani universities, and held posts at Osaka, Otemae, Nagoya, and Ryukoku universities, as well as the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Yasusaburo Sakaki was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1899). He taught Gikyo Ito and held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1906) and Kyushu University (~1906–1925).
Yasushi Endo is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He has held academic posts at Nagoya University, Shitennoji University (attested 2000), and Aichi Bunkyo University (attested 2000–2004).

Yasutaka Muroya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He was a project research associate at the University of Vienna and the University of Leipzig, and later a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Yasutoshi Murakami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1960–1969). He held positions at Yamaguchi University (~1978–2004), Koyasan University (~2004–2012), and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

Yelena Rudenko works in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, Delhi University, and R. B. Suleimenov Institute of Oriental Studies, she held research and lecturing posts at the Suleimenov Institute, Al-Farabi University, and the Kazakh National Academy.
Yellava Subbarayalu is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has served as a professor at Tamil University and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (attested 2015).

Yeshe Thupten is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who taught Daniel Cozort, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and Joe Bransford Wilson. In 1982, he held posts at Middlebury College and as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia.

Yeshi Donden was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. He founded Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961, serving as its director until 1966, and taught Marsha Woolf, Elisabeth Finckh, and Eliot Tokar.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and taught Huidi Zeng.

Yifa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at National Taiwan University, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Yale University. She founded the Woodenfish Foundation and held posts at the University of the West and Harvard University.
Yifan Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. As of 2026, he is a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock. He taught Whitney Cox and Roy Tzohar and became an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2014.

Yijie Tang was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University (~1947–1951). He later served as a professor at Peking University (~1980–2014), held a post at Stanford, and founded the International Academy of Chinese Culture.

Yiliang Zhou was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Educated at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University, and Harvard University, he also studied under Yinke Chen and served as a professor at Peking University (~1952–2001).
Yiling Hua is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at Waseda University (2020–2024) and became a lecturer at Kunming University of Science and Technology in 2024.

Ying-Kuang Chu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School and under Nordan Hutuktu, Nona Hutuktu, Bai Puren, and Gangkar Rinpoche, and later taught Shek-Wing Tam and Yui Chi Lau.

Ying-shih Yü was a sinologist and historian educated at Yenching, New Asia College, CUHK, Kansai, and Harvard. He held professorships at Harvard, CUHK, Yale, and Princeton, and taught Daniel Aaron Getz and Fu-shih Lin.

Yinggang Sun is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He has held positions at Fudan University (attested 2014) and as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
